name: Rock Room (Muldjord) v2
character: big rock/metal kit: Tama Superstar, two rides, two crashes and a china, ambience mics up for a large room sound

source.library: MuldjordKit (sfz port v1.0 of the DrumGizmo kit)
source.author: Lars Muldjord / DrumGizmo team

source.credit_line: Drums: MuldjordKit by Lars Muldjord / DrumGizmo.org, CC BY 4.0 ("Drum samples provided by DrumGizmo.org"); samples mixed, trimmed and re-encoded.
source.modifications: selected hits mixed from 16 mono mic channels to stereo, trimmed, levelled and encoded to MP3 (changes must be indicated under CC BY 4.0)

format.codec: mp3 (LAME VBR -q:a 4, joint stereo or mono; air files -q:a 6)
format.channels: per stroke: see strokes.<drum>.<art>.channels (kick and snare are MONO files to be panned by the engine with strokes.*.pan; everything else is stereo)

core.loads: first; this is the v1-equivalent set (files in the kit root, named <drum>_<articulation>_<layer>_<roundrobin>.mp3 exactly like v1)

detail.loads: in idle time or per stroke on demand (files under x/): the remaining levels, extra takes, extra articulations and the stereo air files

compat.note: The top-level "drums" object has the v1 manifest shape and lists ONLY the core tier, so a v1 loader (file name = <drum>_<art>_<layer>_<rr>.mp3, layers soft->loud) reads this kit unchanged. The full depth is in "strokes": every level of every stroke with its takes; a take with tier "core" is the same file the core view lists (core_layer = its v1 layer number).
differences_from_v1: kick and snare files are mono (pan them; see strokes.<drum>.<art>.pan). A v1 loader plays them centred, which is within 0.2 pan of the recorded position
every take of a level is trimmed to the level median (take_trim), so round robins of one layer differ in tone, not in loudness
layer numbering of the core view is contiguous but the layers are a subset of the full ladder (v2_level gives the ladder index)

dynamics.note: As v1: files of softer levels are quieter and darker as played. stored_rel_db is the level of a level in the files relative to the loudest; natural_rel_db is what was recorded; gain_trim_db (= natural - stored, zero or negative) restores it. Pick the level by velocity (vel_lo/vel_hi or nearest natural_rel_db), blend to the neighbour, do not add a velocity gain law on top.
dynamics.levels: A level is a group of real hits whose 250 ms RMS lies within 1.5 dB; neighbouring levels are at least 1 dB apart. Nothing is synthesised or scaled to make a level.
dynamics.strict: strict=true marks the levels that form a strictly rising chain in BOTH level and brightness (shells: power-weighted spectral centroid of the first 46 ms; hats/cymbals: amplitude-weighted centroid of the first 372 ms). strict=false levels are real hits whose brightness does not rise with level (normal for cymbals, brushes and off-centre hits); keep them for realism or drop them for a strictly monotonic ladder.
dynamics.zone: snare levels are tagged ghost (<= -16 dB under the loudest), soft, medium, accent. Ghost notes should use the ghost-zone levels: they are the softest REAL strokes, not attenuated loud ones.
dynamics.hand: takes of snare, tom and hat levels are tagged R/L: within a level the brighter half of the takes is R (leading hand), the darker half L. This is an assignment made from the takes, not a recorded sticking, unless source.true_hands says otherwise. Alternate L/R on fast figures, repeat R on the beat.
dynamics.art_rel_db: natural level of the loudest level of an articulation relative to the main articulation of the same drum
dynamics.air: snare strokes are mono (close + overheads + room folded to their principal component). air files hold what the fold removed (the decorrelated stereo overhead/room image). To restore the kit-in-a-room width play the air file of the nearest zone under the hit with gain_db = (hit natural_rel_db - air natural_rel_db) + air gain_trim_db - boost_db relative to the hit file gain. side_rel_db is its level under the hit.

memory.budget_note: decoded float32: seconds x channels x 4 bytes x sample rate. Decode per stroke on demand; strokes.<drum>.<art>.decoded_mb_44k gives the cost of each stroke per tier.
memory.mono_trade: Kick and snare carry most of the depth, so they are stored mono: half the decoded memory and download. Measured cost: the stereo residual of the fold is stereo_residual_db (kick about -15 to -20 dB, snare about -10 to -14 dB under the hit), i.e. the hit itself is unchanged and only the diffuse overhead/room width is lost; the air files give it back for the snare at 6 small files per stroke. Hats, cymbals and toms stay stereo (their residual is only 1-9 dB down: folding them would audibly collapse the kit).

engine_made.note: Articulations no source in this kit recorded as its own stroke. The engine builds them at play time from REAL takes listed in strokes; nothing here is a file. Each entry says when to use it (only if the kit has no real stroke of that kind) and is to be labelled engine-made in any UI.

ghost.use: snare.center levels with zone=ghost (the softest real strokes of the source). Never attenuate a louder level to make a ghost.
ghost.when_zone_missing: if a kit has no ghost-zone level, use the softest level with: gain -4 dB, one-pole low-pass at 6.5 kHz, tail shortened with an exponential fade (time constant 90 ms) from 40 ms after the onset. Mark as engine-made.
ghost.takes: rotate takes, prefer hand L on off-beat ghosts, never the same take twice in a row

flam.recipe: grace note = a take of snare.center from the level 10-14 dB under the main note (hand L, a different take from the main note), started 15-30 ms before the main note: 30 ms at velocity <= 60 falling linearly to 15 ms at velocity >= 112; grace gain an extra -2 dB; main note unchanged (hand R)

drag.recipe: two grace notes from the ghost zone of snare.center, two different takes (hands L then L, or L then R for a ruff), at -2d and -d before the main note with d = 25-35 ms (d = min(35 ms, a 64th note at the current tempo, not under 22 ms)); first grace 1.5 dB softer than the second; main note unchanged
drag.three_stroke_ruff: same with three graces at -3d,-2d,-d, d = 22-28 ms, rising 1 dB per grace

buzz.recipe: multiple-bounce press: the main take, then 5-7 takes from the ghost zone at intervals starting at 24 ms and shrinking by x0.82 each, each bounce 2.5 dB softer than the last, every bounce a different take, low-pass 9 kHz on the bounces, whole figure faded over the note length

roll.real_stroke_if_present: snare.roll sustain beds (jazz-virtuosity2); snare.stir / snare.flutter for brushes
roll.recipe: open roll: alternate R/L takes on 32nd notes, level following a random walk of +/-1 level around the written velocity, accents on the written notes

rimshot_substitute.recipe: studio-drs2: snare.center top level + snare.rimclick top level started together, rimclick at -5 dB: an approximation, clearly weaker than a recorded rimshot. rock-muldjord2: no rim sound in the source; use the top snare.center level +1.5 dB and keep the label 'accent', not 'rimshot'.

hat_half_and_pedal_substitute.recipe: half-open: hat.open take of the same level with a 160-220 ms choke envelope (time constant 60 ms). pedal: hat.closed levels 1-2 with the tail faded after 70 ms, -3 dB. Mark as engine-made.

hands.recipe: sticking from the pattern (R on strong subdivisions, alternate on 16ths and fills); choose takes tagged with that hand; L takes are the darker half of each level. True recorded L/R hands exist in no source used here.

general.round_robin: random without immediate repeat inside the hand group
general.level_pick: nearest natural_rel_db to the wanted level, equal-power blend with the neighbour when between two levels

hat.note: a closed, tight or pedal hit stops any ringing open/half/loose/splash voice (fade about 30-60 ms)

missing: hat pedal/half-open/tight/loose/splash (source has closed and open only; see engine_made)

steps: multi-mic stems summed with the gains in mix (same recipe as v1)
close mono mics panned to the position of the drum in the overhead image; polarity of shell close mics chosen for most low end

start trimmed to 1.1 ms before the onset (so the decoded MP3 starts within 1.5 ms), 0.7 ms fade-in; tail cut 54 dB under the loudest hit of the stroke or at max_len_s (a softer hit never rings longer than the loudest), cos^2 fade-out
every candidate hit of the source is measured after mixing; levels are formed from the measured RMS, takes trimmed to the level median (<= 0.75 dB)
no EQ, no compression, no reverb, no pitch change
TPDF dither to 16 bit, LAME VBR
